title: Slow-Season Moves That Actually Pay Off
meta: Free and cheap winter moves ranked by payoff — and the stuff not to waste a dollar on. A no-BS guide for contractors in the slow season.
short: The winter moves worth your time, ranked — and what to skip.
statLabel: beats paid for most winter moves

body.answer: Ranked by payoff: stack reviews, finish your Google profile, fix your site, set up missed-call text-back. All free or cheap. Skip the rebrand and the lead mills.
body.html:
Winter tempts contractors into two traps: doing nothing, or blowing money on shiny stuff that doesn't book jobs. Neither pays. Here's the honest ranking of what actually moves the needle in the slow season — free and cheap stuff first, because free usually beats paid here.

Work the list top to bottom. Each one compounds into spring. For the broader slow-season game plan, read surviving the slow season.

body.h2: Top payoff: reviews and your Google profile
body.answer: Stacking reviews and finishing your Google Business Profile are the highest-payoff, lowest-cost moves you can make all winter.
body.html:
Number one: reviews. Go back through this year and ask every happy customer. Most homeowners read online reviews before choosing a contractor, and most won't seriously consider a shop under 4 stars (BrightLocal Local Consumer Review Survey), so this directly decides who gets the call. Cost: a few texts. Payoff: huge. Start with how to get more Google reviews and the reviews hub.

Number two: finish your Google Business Profile. It's free and it's the biggest local lead source there is. Walk the Google Business Profile checklist for contractors and fill in every field, with real photos.

body.h2: Solid payoff: site fixes and missed-call text-back
body.answer: Fix the five things on your site and turn on missed-call text-back. Cheap, fast, and they stop you leaking leads come spring.
body.html:
Number three: fix your website. Phone above the fold, fast load, clear service area, real photos, a reason to call. Most of it's free and you can do it in the slow weeks.

Number four: missed-call text-back. It's cheap and it stops you losing leads to voicemail when spring volume hits. Speed wins jobs — responding in 5 minutes instead of 30 makes you up to 100x more likely to connect with a lead (Lead Response Management study, Prof. James Oldroyd). Set it up via missed-call text-back for contractors and speed to lead.

body.answer: Don't blow the slow season on a rebrand, a fancy new logo, or shared-lead mills. Tie any spend to cost-per-booked-job.
body.html:
Now the don'ts. Don't spend the slow season on a rebrand or a new logo. It feels productive and books zero jobs. Don't pour money into shared-lead mills that sell the same lead four times — the FTC fined HomeAdvisor/Angi $7.2 million (FTC, 2023), and your real cost per booked job on those is uglier than the sticker.

Any dollar you do spend should tie to cost per booked job, not a vibe — see contractor marketing budget. And on anything with a tax angle, ask your accountant. If you'd rather a human sort the worth-it from the waste, talk to Aaron.

faq.q: What's the single best slow-season move?
faq.a: Stacking reviews from this year's happy customers. It costs a few texts and reviews decide who gets the call in spring.

faq.q: Should I rebrand during the slow season?
faq.a: No. A new logo feels productive and books no jobs. Spend the time on reviews, your Google profile, and your site instead.

faq.q: Are lead-buying sites worth it in winter?
faq.a: Usually not. They sell the same lead to several shops, so your real cost per booked job is high. Build owned assets first and track the math.
